topics.name: Field Service Management Fundamentals
topics.description: Field service types, modules and industry use cases, solution features, process lifecycle, personas, roles, work order initiation and delivery, mobile application usage, and agent skills and schedules

introduction.overview: Field Service Management Fundamentals covers the core concepts of ServiceNow FSM, including field service types, industry-specific use cases, and the complete work order lifecycle from initiation through delivery and confirmation.
introduction.keyConcepts: Field Service Management (FSM) enables organizations to manage field service operations including work orders, dispatch, scheduling, and mobile workforce management. The solution supports various field service types and industry use cases. Key personas include dispatchers who coordinate work assignments, field agents who execute tasks, and customers who receive services. The work order lifecycle encompasses initiation, qualification, scheduling, dispatch, delivery, and confirmation stages.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain carries the highest exam weight because understanding FSM fundamentals is essential for successful implementation. You must understand the complete work order lifecycle, personas involved, and how the mobile application enables field agents to fulfill work orders efficiently.

topics.name: Implementation Planning
topics.description: Preparation activities, stakeholders, good practices, ServiceNow maturity levels, and integrations with applications and data sources

introduction.overview: Implementation Planning covers the preparation activities and best practices for successful FSM implementation, including stakeholder identification, maturity assessment, and integration planning.
introduction.keyConcepts: Successful FSM implementation requires careful planning including stakeholder identification, assessment of ServiceNow maturity levels, and planning for integrations with external applications and data sources. The Guided Setup provides a structured approach to configuration. Prerequisites and requirements must be understood before beginning implementation.
introduction.whyItMatters: While this domain has a small exam weight, understanding implementation planning helps ensure successful FSM deployments. Questions may focus on preparation activities, stakeholder roles, and integration considerations.

topics.name: Implementing Field Service Processes
topics.description: Foundational data configuration, field service business processes, work order templates, workforce management, preventive maintenance, inventory management, scheduling methods, dispatcher workspace, appointment booking, time recording, and labor rate cards

introduction.overview: Implementing Field Service Processes is the largest exam domain, covering the detailed configuration of FSM including foundational data, work order templates, scheduling optimization, inventory management, and workforce configuration.
introduction.keyConcepts: FSM implementation requires configuring foundational data (locations, groups, users, customer accounts, contacts, stockrooms, assets), work order templates with task dependencies, SMART assessments for questionnaires, workforce management including agent skills and schedules, preventive maintenance plans, inventory management with part sourcing and transfers, and various scheduling methods including schedule optimization, dynamic scheduling, and route optimization. The Dispatcher Workspace provides centralized control for work assignment and monitoring.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain carries the highest exam weight because process configuration is the core of FSM implementation. You must understand how to configure all aspects of field service operations from foundational data through advanced scheduling and inventory management.

topics.name: Implementing Related Processes
topics.description: Agent feedback and tracking, targeted communications, contextual knowledge, and Now Agent mobile application setup and usage

introduction.overview: Implementing Related Processes covers the configuration of supporting features including agent feedback, communications, knowledge integration, and the Now Agent mobile application.
introduction.keyConcepts: Related processes enhance the core FSM functionality through agent feedback and tracking mechanisms, targeted communications via push notifications and SMS, contextual knowledge integration for field agents, and the Now Agent mobile application which enables offline capabilities for field workers.
introduction.whyItMatters: While this domain has a small exam weight, these related processes are important for a complete FSM implementation. Understanding mobile application setup, offline capabilities, and communication features supports field agent effectiveness.
